sources.entry: How to ask good questions, Julia Evans.

summary.title: How to ask good questions
summary.one_liner: Learn practical techniques for asking technical questions that get useful answers, such as stating your understanding first, asking fact-based questions, and choosing who to ask.
keywords: how to ask questions the smart way
mentoring and learning on the job
takeaways: State your current understanding and ask 'is that right?' to get corrected quickly and specifically.
Ask narrow questions whose answers are concrete facts rather than vague topics like 'how do SQL joins work?'.
Admit what you don't understand and ask for clarification; confident engineers do this often.
Before asking, research a little, and weigh whether the person's time is well spent and whether they are too senior for the question.
Asking good questions and answering questions are both valuable contributions to a community.
summary.summary: Julia Evans shares guidelines drawn from her experience as a software engineer for asking better technical questions. She argues that asking imperfect questions is fine, and recommends techniques like stating your understanding and asking if it is right, asking fact-based questions, saying what you don't understand, and building a glossary of unfamiliar terms. The post also covers doing light research first, choosing whom to ask based on timing and seniority, asking strangers online, asking questions that reveal hidden assumptions, and answering questions as a way to contribute. It is anecdotal and illustrated with examples from rkt, Docker, SQL joins, and her data team onboarding.
